title: Dancing guitarist and the paralyzed trumpeter from Buddy Bolden's days
summary: Dangerous old days; a trumpeter whose name Miller cannot recall, said to be paralyzed after a woman's curse, linked to Bolden.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Well, I guess a lot of people used to do all kind of things in those days.

Boysmen. Well, we had a guitar player. I'll forget that boy's name. But he had a knack of five or six women's at a dance with Jack Kerrin in. Playing at National Park. Boy, that was a jumping spot. And he danced five and six girls there. And he's bigoted like, you know. He's nice looking, but he's bigoted. I can't call his name. You go ahead, I'll see you tomorrow. You go ahead, I'll see you. And all that. Kept on with that stuff. But one of them guys, I pardoned him. He sold up like that. Don't nobody know what happened. Who killed him? Yeah, they pardoned the devil in them days, did you?
They said that about Buddy Bolden, too.

And there's another trumpet player. I didn't get the scene. But it's Buddy Bolden days. But I know, yes, I did get the scene. When I got the scene, he was paralyzed. And they say a woman told him he was going to kick her down the step in the condom home. And she told him if he kicked her down the step, he'll never use that arm and hand no more. And that's the truth. That leg either. He kicked her down the dog if he wasn't. Got a fella I've drunk ever since. Some old trumpet player. I don't know who he was. Yes, I do know his name, too. But I can't call it now.
Was he from Uptown or down?
Hot dog. That man named Ray Clem. It'll come to you later.
